requirement_summary: Learning History Migration: Schema/registry/knowledge-store migration 시 candidate lifecycle, lineage, old decisions, revoked assets, qualification evidence를 보존한다. migration 후 history loss가 있으면 reconstructability PASS 금지.
subject: src/main/java/kr/co/oruda/onsure/platform/SemanticAssuranceV2WorkflowService.java (learningHistoryMigrationCheck), assurance.learning.history-migration.check v2 operation; contracts/learning-history-migration-check.v1.schema.json (NEW, built this pass)
observed_source: SemanticAssuranceV2DispatcherBridgeTest (real dispatch through the full RBAC/workflow chain)
coverage_notes: decision is computed for real across all 5 named categories (candidate lifecycle, lineage, old decisions, revoked assets, qualification evidence): every category is checked for post_migration_count < pre_migration_count (a real pre/post comparison JSON Schema cannot express), and ANY single lossy category forces RECONSTRUCTABILITY_BLOCKED for the whole migration, naming every lossy category by exact pre->post delta -- a caller cannot claim overall preservation while one category quietly lost records. All 5 required categories must be present (not a subset) or the check itself is rejected as incomplete.
open_gap: Checks record COUNTS per category, not content-level integrity (e.g. a record could survive migration with the same count but corrupted/altered content) -- a full content-digest comparison per record is a stronger, disclosed follow-on. This operation trusts the caller-supplied pre/post counts as given; it does not itself query the real pre- and post-migration stores (no such migration has actually run in this codebase yet to observe).
design_reference_gap: REQUIREMENT_WITHOUT_DESIGN: the trace scanner correctly excludes the requirement's own authority document (153_LEARNING_VALIDATION_GOVERNANCE_SOVEREIGNTY_AND_SUPPLY_CHAIN_REFINEMENT.md) as circular, and no other design document currently elaborates this specific mechanism -- a genuine, disclosed gap.
